rationale: MercariPriceBandCollector.Collect (src/MarketMakerEtl.Core/Services/MercariPriceBandCollector.cs) is split into a thin MercariPriceBandCollector (constructs a SearchPageFetcher and delegates) and a new PriceBandCollectionRun that owns one run's worker pool -- splitting was required to stay under CI0014's 200-effective-line class cap once the concurrent loop and its locking were added. PriceBandQueue.Dequeue/EnqueueChildren/Count and the run's merged dictionary, running counters (Fetched/BandsPruned/BandsOverCapacityUnsplit/TotalReported, now held on a new CollectorRunState) and _searchPageFailures list are all mutated only inside a single CollectorRunState.SyncRoot lock; only the actual network fetch (SearchPageFetcher.Fetch) and, for a backfill run, SoldBackfillPlanner.Resolve's own network calls happen outside that lock, which is where the concurrency saves wall-clock time. A configurable number of worker Tasks (Math.Max(1, MercariCollectionSettings.SearchConcurrency), new record field defaulting to 1 so every existing positional-construction call site in MercariPriceBandCollectorTests keeps its old, order-sensitive NSubstitute Returns(...) sequencing and keeps compiling and passing unchanged) each loop: atomically claim-and-dequeue the next band under the lock (only when Fetched < MaxBandsPerDirection and the queue is non-empty, incrementing Fetched at claim time so the band cap counts fetches issued, not completed, exactly as the ticket requires), fetch it unlocked, then re-acquire the lock only to merge/prune/split/store via the extracted static BandOutcomeApplier (ProcessSearchOutcome / ApplyBackfillDecision / MergeAndCountNew / ShouldSplit, moved out of PriceBandCollectionRun into their own static class purely to keep PriceBandCollectionRun's own line count under the CI0014 cap -- no behavior change). A split's children are only ever enqueued from inside this same lock, after that band's own fetch has completed, so 'a split's children join the queue when their parent's result arrives' holds exactly as before; with SearchConcurrency=1 (every existing test's implicit default) the single worker's claim/fetch/merge sequence is byte-for-byte the old sequential while-loop, which is why all 294 pre-existing MercariPriceBandCollectorTests/SoldBackfillPlannerTests/SearchPageServiceTests cases pass unmodified. SoldBackfillPlanner (src/MarketMakerEtl.Core/Services/SoldBackfillPlanner.cs) is now safe to have its single shared instance's Resolve() called concurrently by different bands' worker tasks in the same run (unavoidable once bands run concurrently, since one SoldBackfillPlanner is shared for the whole sold direction): the per-listing date cache changed from Dictionary<string, DateLookup> to a lock-guarded Dictionary<string, Task<DateLookup>> (the standard async-memoization pattern -- a listing's date is fetched at most once even if two concurrent Resolve() calls or probes ask for it at the same time), and _itemPageFetches changed from a plain int++ to Interlocked.Increment/Volatile.Read so the fetch budget check/count can't race. Resolve gained a trailing optional 'int concurrency = 1' parameter (after the existing CancellationToken, so no existing SoldBackfillPlannerTests call site needed to change) that MercariPriceBandCollector now passes _settings.SearchConcurrency into; it is threaded through FindCutoff into a new ProbeMargin that fetches every position in the +/-3 probe window concurrently (via a SemaphoreSlim(concurrency) gate and Task.WhenAll, aggregating with the same order-independent Math.Max as before) -- this is safe to parallelize with zero behavior change because ProbeMargin already unconditionally visits every position in that window regardless of what it finds, so concurrency only changes the order fetches happen in, never the count or the result. The binary search in FindCutoff, and the leading-sample short-circuit in IsEntirelyBeforeCutoff plus the single 'oldest' (last item) fetch in Resolve, are deliberately left sequential: both currently early-exit to save fetches (IsEntirelyBeforeCutoff stops sampling as soon as one leading item isn't before the cutoff; Resolve skips fetching the last item at all when IsEntirelyBeforeCutoff already returned true), and SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_still_report_none_when_the_first_three_items_all_resolve_before_the_cutoff asserts an exact ItemPageFetchesUsed of 3 for that short-circuit -- parallelizing across that boundary would add extra, sometimes-wasted fetches and change budget consumption in ways the ticket's 'must not change backfill decisions' constraint (and this locked-in test) rule out. This is a deliberate, narrower reading of scope item 2's 'the first and last item of a page' than a literal one; see Gaps in the PR. ScrapeOptions gained SearchConcurrency (default 3, src/MarketMakerEtl.Core/Models/Scraper/ScrapeOptions.cs), read from Scrape:SearchConcurrency via ServiceCollectionExtensions.BuildScrapeOptions/ReadInt, and SearchPageService.CollectDirection now passes _options.SearchConcurrency into MercariCollectionSettings alongside the other per-run tuning knobs.
declaredRedTestsNote: The new collector test builds a deterministic, URL-addressable fake catalogue (reusing the existing CatalogueUrlService/CatalogueParser test doubles already in MercariPriceBandCollectorTests, which decode a price band straight from the request URL rather than depending on call order) so that a concurrency-3 run and a concurrency-1 run over the exact same fake data are guaranteed to visit the same final set of bands and merge the same listings regardless of fetch ordering -- the band budget (60) is set comfortably above the ~24 fetches the catalogue actually needs so neither run hits the band cap, which is what makes the two runs' final merged-listing sets provably order-independent rather than dependent on which bands happen to get processed before a cap-driven early stop. A new ConcurrencyTrackingScrapeClient fake records the maximum number of concurrently in-flight GetPageHtml calls (via Interlocked/CAS) behind a 20ms artificial delay, proving overlap occurred (Is.GreaterThan(1)) and was never exceeded (Is.LessThanOrEqualTo(concurrencyLimit)). No existing declared/red test needed to change; all 294 pre-existing MarketMakerEtl.Tests.Unit cases pass unmodified because every existing MercariCollectionSettings/SoldBackfillPlanner construction site implicitly gets SearchConcurrency/concurrency=1, preserving the old fully-sequential code path byte-for-byte.
